newsitem.title: USA: Fluor falls as analysts downgrade stock.
newsitem.headline: Fluor falls as analysts downgrade stock.

text.p: Shares of Fluor Corp dropped sharply Friday after several analysts downgraded the stock, citing lack of confidence in the company's focus.
Fluor was off 6-1/2 to 58 and was one of the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.
At a meeting with Wall Street analysts Thursday, Fluor management failed to provide a clear message about their plans to refocus the company, analysts said.
"In today's world, the absence of clarity certainly warrants investor caution," said Richard Rossi, an analyst with Dean Witter.
Rossi said he downgraded Fluor to neutral from buy, trimmed his 1997 earnings estimate to $3.40 a share from $3.60, and cut his 1998 estimate to $4.00 from $4.30.
Oppenheimer & Co cut the stock to market perform from buy, while Smith Barney downgraded Fluor to neutral from outperform, saying its "confidence in Fluor management has slipped."
Analysts said it appears Fluor does not have a clear plan to address the problems that plagued its first quarter performance.
In that quarter, Fluor earned $0.73 a share, falling short of Wall Street expectations of $0.78. The company blamed cost overruns at two fixed-price power projects.
Fluor recently said it planned to trim $100 million from its engineering and construction cost structure by 1998. But analysts were not impressed, saying the plan sounded vague and non-specific.
The cost-cutting plan will "keep things from deteriorating, but apparently little of that $100 million will drop to the bottom line," Merrill Lynch analyst Jeanne Terrile said in a research report.
Merrill advised investors to avoid Fluor until the fundamental cost issues are resolved.
Some analysts suggested that Fluor management has been distracted by efforts to expand globally.
Analysts said the company's long-term prospects remain promising, but they questioned its near-term earnings reliability.
Irvine, Calif.-based Fluor is an engineering, construction and diversified services company with an investment in low-sulphur coal.
Fluor officials could not be reached for comment.
